messages:
andrew: Customer reports frequent mid-stream SSE disconnects when switching WiFi -> cellular. Client sees partial output, then reconnects and sometimes gets truncated or duplicated tokens. Happening on iOS app v2.3.4. Request-id: rq_0a9f3c.

maria: Repro details from customer: iPhone 13, iOS 16.5, using EventSource polyfill (EventSource when on wifi, fallback to xhr-streaming). Error event fires immediately after network change. Stack snippet: `EventSource#onerror -> connection closed`. They attached network logs showing TCP FIN right after the switch.

andrew: Ok — can you paste the exact curl we can run and the server logs around rq_0a9f3c? Need to repro locally first. Also confirm whether they hit our hosted API or dedicated.

maria: Hosted (prod). curl they used (redacted token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-2-x"
```
Server side snippet from logs (time order):
```
[2026-03-14T15:12:02Z] rq_0a9f3c: conn established
[2026-03-14T15:12:27Z] rq_0a9f3c: wrote partial tokens (streaming)
[2026-03-14T15:12:43Z] rq_0a9f3c: client disconnected (read error: connection reset by peer)
[2026-03-14T15:12:44Z] rq_0a9f3c: new request from same client, 200 OK
```
kevin: This smells like NAT/idle timeouts or an ALB/proxy closing connections when the device switches networks. Mobile handoff tends to produce TCP FINs. Do we currently emit SSE comment keepalives? That prevents idle proxies from closing the socket.

elena: We recently tightened some proxy idle timeouts to 60s in prod to reduce dangling connections. If tokens are generated slowly (model cold start or long reasoning), 60s might be hit.

kevin: Short-term mitigation: emit SSE comment pings every 10-15s from the runtime. SSE comment format is `: keepalive\n\n` which proxies don't forward as events but it counts as traffic. Also consider bumping ALB idle timeout to 120s for edge pool handling mobile clients.

maria: Customer confirms token emission frequency can be >20s in some prompts (we're seeing slow steps). Will staging patch help us prove it?

andrew: Yes — enable keepalive on staging and run the customer's prompt loop while doing a WiFi -> cellular toggle repeatedly. Also capture tcpdump on client device if possible.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: runtime/stayalive-pings -> staging (build 1847.1). :rocket:

kevin: Patch for reference (Go runtime handler):
```go
w.Write([]byte(": keepalive\\n\\n"))
w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
// start token stream goroutine
```
This sends repo-friendly comments and keeps ALBs from idling.

maria: After running ~30 minutes on staging with repeated toggles, disconnects dropped from ~6/min to 0. We saw one weird case where client reconnected and resumed, but the app UI showed duplicated tokens (same content twice).

kevin: Expected — our current semantics treat reconnect as a new request; we don't support server-side stream resume. Client reconnect => new model run unless client passes an idempotency/session token we can map. We need to avoid double-applying partial outputs on reconnect.

elena: Any resume API adds complexity + security (mapping resume token -> user context). We can prototype a short lived stream session id tied to the auth token and request-id, TTL 60s, signed. But that's mid-term.

andrew: Short term, propose client-side dedupe: app keeps last N tokens hash and drops immediate duplicates on reconnect for X seconds. Also suggest we add a `x-stream-session: <uuid>` header that the client can optionally send; if present we can attempt best-effort dedupe on server logs and console.

maria: Customer is OK to implement client dedupe quickly. They asked if we can also expose a connection-liveness heartbeat event so they can detect partial finalization earlier.

kevin: We can add a `:keepalive` comment and also emit a small event `event: ping\ndata: {"t":"keepalive"}\\n\\n` if they want visible pings. That won't change semantics but helps client detect liveness.

elena: Track action items: 1) prod: enable keepalive pings for edge pool and bump ALB to 120s (ops). 2) infra: monitor for regressions from increased idle timeouts. 3) runtime: consider session resume design doc (security + TTL). 4) support: share client dedupe guidance + sample code.

andrew: Sample client dedupe pseudo: keep lastTokenHash; on reconnect drop tokens where sha256(token)==lastTokenHash for first 500ms of new stream. Simple and effective.

maria: Customer will ship client dedupe and rerun tests tomorrow morning. Can support please reply with recommended header `x-stream-session` format and a small example they can add?

kevin: Recommended optional header: `x-stream-session: <uuid-v4>` — server will log it and in future we can use it to map resumes. For now it's just helpful for tracing. Example: `x-stream-session: 3f8a7b2e-9f3c-4d2a-a8f1-2c9f3b7d4a1c`.

andrew: Closing loop — I'll inform customer, attach staging logs showing keepalive behavior, and schedule a short follow-up call if they still see issues after client dedupe. Thanks everyone for quick triage. :white_check_mark:
